Subject: Request: extended net terms + escrow option for pilot

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looked promising for our triage workflows. Procurement has asked me to formalize a ask on payment flexibility for the pilot phase. Two constraints on our side:

- Cashflow timing across multiple subsidiaries means Net60 would be easiest for us.
- Legal wants either (A) a short-term escrow arrangement that releases monthly on acceptance of milestones, or (B) a conditional holdback tied to usage thresholds so we can ramp without a large upfront deposit.

Can Redwood accommodate Net60 for the first 90 days if we put a 10% milestone escrow (released monthly on delivery targets)? If not, would you consider Net45 with a 2% early-pay discount and a credit line cap that scales with usage?

I attached our standard procurement checklist and a sample escrow instruction (procurement attachments).

Looking for quick confirmation so we can get legal and finance aligned.

Best,
Sophie Miller
Head of Procurement, Imperia Health
procurement@imperiahealth.com

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the docs. Quick read-through and proposed path forward below.

Short answer: we can be flexible, but need to balance credit exposure with operational risk. Proposed options (from our side):

1) Conditional Net60 + escrow: We can accept Net60 for a 90-day pilot if Imperia puts 10% of the estimated pilot spend into a third-party escrow that releases monthly against agreed acceptance criteria. Redwood would require a minimal non-refundable onboarding fee to cover GPU reservation.

2) Net45 + early pay discount: If escrow is not acceptable, we can do Net45 with a 2% early-pay discount (payment within 15 days) and an initial credit cap that ramps to full consumption after 60 days of on-time payments.

3) Hybrid: Net60 for first 30 days, automatic move to Net45 once a usage threshold is crossed (e.g., 250k tokens/month) and no outstanding invoices.

Next steps I suggest:
- I'll loop in Finance (Marissa) to confirm the credit application/thresholds.
- Karthik can provide the suggested contract language for escrow and holdback.
- If Imperia agrees, we can draft a mutual action plan and DocuSign the payment schedule.

I'll attach a draft payment schedule that maps the three options side-by-side. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Sophie / Jonas — looping Finance in with concrete guardrails. A few clarifications from our side before we sign off on Net60:

- Credit assessment: We need the completed credit application (attached) plus 12 months of AP aging or payment references.
- Deposit/escrow: If Imperia prefers escrow, Redwood requires the escrow agent to be an approved third party and the release schedule to map to specific, measurable milestones (we can provide the acceptance checklist).
- VAT/tax routing: For clarity on VAT reclaim and where invoice liability sits, please confirm which Imperia legal entity will sign and where VAT is registered. If the billing entity is outside the US (EU subsidiary), we'll need the VAT reg number to zero-rate exports where applicable.
- Credit cap: For Net45 or Net60 options we propose a starting cap equal to 1.5x forecasted monthly spend, reviewed after 45 days.

If you can return the credit app and the vat/legal entity info by Friday, we can finalize the payment schedule and get a minimal onboarding invoice processed.

Thanks,

Sophie — adding proposed contract snippets for the escrow and volume-triggered credit ramp. Key points we want in the SOW/payment section:

- Escrow instruction clause: "Upon execution of this Agreement, the Customer shall deposit 10% of the estimated 90-day pilot spend into an escrow account managed by [Escrow Agent]. Funds shall be released monthly upon Redwood's written acceptance of the monthly acceptance checklist. Any disputed acceptance amounts shall be resolved per Section 7 (Dispute Resolution)."

- Volume-trigger clause: "If Customer consumption exceeds 250,000 tokens in any 30-day period, Customer's credit cap shall automatically increase by 50% for the subsequent 60 days, subject to no overdue invoices. Redwood will notify Customer within five business days of any cap change."

- VAT handling: "Invoices to Customer's EU legal entity shall include the Customer's valid VAT ID. Where applicable and supported by documentation, Redwood will zero-rate exports and the Customer remains responsible for local VAT reporting."

Please see attached doc with redlines. These are intended to be a starting point — happy to take Imperia's redlines.

Regards,
